reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g1_mg_q1_2), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample packet thoroughly fulfills the MATATAG competency requirement to 'Compose and decompose triangles, squares, and rectangles.' Items assess composition, such as combining triangles into rectangles ("Two triangles are placed together, matching their longest straight edges. What shape do they form?") and squares into rectangles ("Two identical squares are placed side by side. What shape do they form?"). They also directly assess decomposition, such as splitting rectangles into squares ("A long rectangle is cut across its width into two equal squares. What two shapes are made?") and splitting squares into triangles ("A square is cut on a slant, from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes are made?").

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The items comprehensively cover the full scope of geometric relationships between triangles, squares, and rectangles. Both composition (combining triangles into a square: "Two identical triangles are joined along their matching straight edges to make a 4-sided shape with equal sides. What shape is formed?"; combining squares into a rectangle: "Two identical squares are placed side by side. What shape do they form?") and decomposition (cutting a rectangle into smaller rectangles: "A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?"; cutting a rectangle into squares: "A long rectangle is cut across its width into two equal squares. What two shapes are made?") are represented across all three specified 2D shapes.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The language and cognitive load are perfectly tuned for Grade 1 Quarter 1 learners. Descriptions rely on clear, concrete physical actions rather than abstract terminology, using intuitive phrasing such as "cut on a slant, from one corner to the opposite corner" and "Two identical squares are placed side by side. What shape do they form?". The visual and spatial logic is straightforward and accessible.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample set demonstrates strong variant breadth, featuring diverse pairings and transformations including triangle-to-rectangle composition ("Two identical triangles are rotated to fit together into a rectangle. What shape is made?"), triangle-to-square composition ("Two identical triangles are joined along their matching straight edges to make a 4-sided shape with equal sides. What shape is formed?"), and rectangle-to-rectangle decomposition ("A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?"), across both standard mcq and read_mcq formats.

competency_alignment.rationale: All sample items remain strictly aligned with the target competency without introducing extraneous concepts or out-of-scope polygons. The items focus squarely on 2D composition and decomposition of triangles, squares, and rectangles (e.g., "Two triangles are placed together, matching their longest straight edges. What shape do they form?" and "A square is cut on a slant, from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes are made?"), avoiding unneeded geometric terminology or multidimensional complexity.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The scale of manipulation involves 2 simple geometric parts (e.g., "A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?", "Two identical squares are placed side by side. What shape do they form?"), which is precisely calibrated for Grade 1 students beginning spatial decomposition and composition.
